joint.outcome: theorem from standard axioms with no shared-scope hypotheses: consistent with every satisfiable law set

law.label: Plateau's second rule: four equal-tension walls meet at arccos(-1/3), about 109.5 degrees
law.statement_en: Where four fluid walls of the same positive tension meet at a point, balance, and make equal angles with one another, each pair meets at arccos(-1/3) (109° 28′, the tetrahedral angle): more than a right angle and less than the 120 degrees of a triple junction. Without the symmetry assumption, the six pairwise cosines still sum to -2.

hypotheses.name: plateau-tetrahedral-angle#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Fluid walls of uniform equal tension in static equilibrium: the vector sum of the four tensions along the wall directions is zero.

hypotheses.name: plateau-tetrahedral-angle#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Equal pairwise angles (the six inner products equal). Plateau's rule also says that in a stable foam exactly four edges meet at a vertex; that stability statement is not formalised here.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model of fluid walls under tension; it applies wherever the walls are such films and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: Exact: four unit vectors balanced under equal positive tension have pairwise cosines summing to -2 (quadJunction_inner_sum).
With all six cosines equal to c0: c0 = -1/3, angle = arccos(-1/3), and π/2 < angle < 2π/3 (tetrahedralJunction_angle).
Non-vacuity: the four unit vectors (±1, ±1, ±1)/√3 with an even number of minus signs (tetrahedralJunction_angle_witness).
assumed: Fluid walls of uniform equal tension in static equilibrium.
Equal pairwise angles; the 'exactly four edges per vertex' stability clause of Plateau's rule is not formalised.

sources: Plateau, Statique expérimentale et théorique des liquides soumis aux seules forces moléculaires (1873), second rule
On Growth and Form (1917), chapter VII (the rhombic-dodecahedron angle of the bee's cell, claim thompson1917-ch07-11, is the same angle)
On Growth and Form (1917), chapter VII
